I expect Alexander Hernandez to be just a bit too aggressive as he gets caught in one of Hoopers submission attempts for an early stoppage. title: Fight By Fight Preview | UFC 319: Du Plessis vs Chimaev
text: The UFC blows into the Windy City for the first time in a little more than six years, returning to the United Center with a packed pay-per-view fight card capped by one of the most highly anticipated bouts of the year. Saturday night’s main event features reigning middleweight champion Dricus Du Plessis defending his title for the second time this year as he steps in with undefeated challenger Khamzat Chimaev, who has been forecasted to reach this position since he first stormed the gates back on Fight Island. Back by a quartet of compelling main card contests and a loaded preliminary card slate, UFC 319 shapes up as one of the deepest, most competitive cards of the year, and we’ve got the goods on what to expect when the action hits the Octagon this weekend below. Main Event: Dricus Du Plessis vs Khamzat Chimaev Location: United Center — Chicago, IL Where to Watch: ESPN+ / Disney+ Other Main Card Matches: Order UFC 319: Du Plessis vs Chimaev Prelim Matches: MIDDLEWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP MAIN EVENT Dricus Du Plessis vs Khamzat Chimaev Middleweight champ Dricus Du Plessis looks to defend his place atop the division once more as he welcomes the challenge of unbeaten marauder Khamzat Chimaev in the UFC 319 main event. The South African titleholder continues to deliver more dominant performances and eliminate room for questioning his standing as the best middleweight in the world with each successive outing. He earned his second successful title defense earlier this year by thoroughly outworking former champ Sean Strickland in a rematch of their UFC 297 encounter, which extended Du Plessis’ record to 9-0 in the UFC and 23-2 overall. Five years after exploding onto the scene with three wins in two months, Chimaev finally lands in his first championship fight, aiming to maintain his unblemished record while proving he’s every bit the unstoppable force many have long believed him to be. The now 31-year-old standout secured this opportunity with a first-round submission win over Robert Whittaker last October that was closer to a mugging than a competitive matchup, and silenced any questions about his health or his ability to hang with the very best in the world. GET YOUR TICKETS: UFC 319 | UFC Shanghai | UFC Paris This is an absolutely fascinating matchup because despite all their successes, there are questions that remain on both sides and cases to be made in favor of each man. More than any fight either has engaged in to this point, Saturday’s main event is going to be the proving ground for both Du Plessis and Chimaev, and have an unquestionable impact on how we look at each in the present and going forward. This is going to be special. ADDITIONAL MAIN CARD MATCHUPS Lerone Murphy vs Aaron Pico Lerone Murphy puts his undefeated record on the line as he welcomes Aaron Pico to the Octagon for the first time in this outstanding featherweight fixture. There are a lot of similarities between Murphy and fellow Brit Leon Edwards, who steadily worked his way to the top of the welterweight division as, like the former welterweight ruler, the 34-year-old Manchester man is on an outstanding run of success without much fanfare, and is without question a better fighter than most understand or give him credit for being. Over his last three fights, “The Miracle” has earned quality wins over Edson Barboza, Dan Ige, and Josh Emmett to cement his standing as a contender, and vanquishing Pico would certainly strengthen his case for a championship opportunity early next year. Now 28 years old, Pico has grown into being the fighter most envisioned when he was a teenage phenom that had yet to actually make the transition into mixed martial arts, though some questions do still linger. He’s gone 9-1 over his last 10 fights, with his only loss coming as a result of an injury, and has a complete assortment of tools at his disposal, including proven knockout power and excellent wrestling. Murphy is the established, entrenched half of this pairing, though he still has room to ascend in terms of acceptance and recognition, and a win here would definitely help that cause. For Pico, this is his chance to catapult himself right into the thick of the title chase and show that he’s more than capable of running with the elites in the UFC featherweight division. Geoff Neal vs Carlos Prates Originally scheduled to face off at UFC 314 in Miami, Geoff Neal and Carlos Prates command the feature slot on Saturday’s talent-rich main card. Neal, who turns 35 less than two weeks after this weekend’s event, competes for the first time since his abbreviated bout with Rafael Dos Anjos last October in Abu Dhabi, which was halted when the former lightweight champ suffered a knee injury. The Fortis MMA representative has been a Top 15 staple for the last several years, settling into life in the 6-12 range, while showcasing sharp, punishing hands and the tenacity and moxie to push both Shavkat Rakhmanov and Ian Machado Garry to their limits. WATCH: UFC 319 Embedded Following a breakout rookie campaign where he went 4-0 with four finishes to force his way into the rankings, Prates suffered his first loss in a dozen fights last time out, dropping a decision to Machado Garry in a fight where the Irish standout was strategic for the majority ofthe contest before getting in a little trouble late. If the Fighting Nerds’ core four — Caio Borralho, Jean Silva, Mauricio Ruffy, and Prates — were the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Prates would be Raphael, the somewhat volatile, ever-dangerous member of the group, which is what makes him a constant threat, captivating to watch, and susceptible to missteps like the one he experienced in Kansas City against Machado Garry. It’s highly likely that these two wade into the center, touch gloves, and start throwing fastballs at one another straight away, stopping only when the horn sounds signaling the end of the round or one of them is left staring up at the lights. Buckle up and enjoy because this one is sure to be electric. Jared Cannonier vs Michael Page Middleweight has been having a moment here, and before the title goes up for grabs, Jared Cannonier and Michael Page will stand opposite one another with a place in the Top 10 hanging in the balance. A Top 10 mainstay since he debuted in the division towards the end of 2018, Cannonier halted a two-fight slide earlier this year by rallying to finish Gregory Rodrigues. Now 26 fights into his career and at “Level 41,” the MMA Lab product is the perfect top-end measuring stick in a weight class that has been undergoing some changes over the last two years, as the only people to best him at middleweight remain former champs Robert Whittaker and Israel Adesanya, and upcoming Paris headliners Nassourdine Imavov and Caio Borralho, who could very well be fighting to determine who faces Saturday’s title fight winner. BREAKING: Paramount and TKO Announce Historic UFC Media Rights Agreement Page bounced up to middleweight earlier this year to bounce Shara Magomedov from the ranks of the unbeaten, showing that he’s the better range fighter of the two and still a tricky puzzle to solve for whomever stands across from him inside the Octagon. While he’s now 38 years old, “MVP” feels like he’s capable of having an extended twilight similar to that of Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson, who has remained a Top 15 fighter well into his 40s. This one is all going to come down to how Cannonier opts to approach things, as it feels like there is a clear blueprint for how to neutralize Page. Typically, “The Killa Gorilla” isn’t someone that looks to wrestle all that much, so we should get plenty of striking exchanges in space, where it will be Cannonier’s power against Page’s speed and variety. Tim Elliott vs Kai Asakura Saturday’s main card kicks off with an intriguing pairing in the flyweight division as former title challengers Tim Elliott and Kai Asakura go head-to-head in Chicago. Nearly a decade removed from his competitive title bout with Demetrious Johnson, Elliott has remained one of the top veteran tests in the 125-pound weight class, posting a 7-6 record over his last 13 starts, most of which have come against the division’s best. He hasn’t fought since submitting Sumudaerji in December 2023, so it will be interesting to see how the 38-year-old looks after such an extended absence. Asakura got an immediate title shot last December after joining the UFC from RIZIN, stepping into a bout with Alexandre Pantoja where he fell by submission in the second round. The Japanese fighter rose to prominence on the strength of quality wins over Manel Kape and KyojiHoriguchi, as well as his explosive power, and he gets a second chance to make a first impression in the Octagon. PRELIMINARY CARD PAIRINGS Baisangur Susurkaev vs Eric Nolan Four days after earning his place on the UFC roster, Baisangur Susurkaev gets his wish to compete this weekend alongside training partner Khamzat Chimaev as he takes on New Jersey native Eric Nolan at UFC 319. Susurkaev earned the lone finish on Tuesday's opening episode of Dana White's Contender Series, finishing returning hopeful Murtaza Talha with a front kick to the bread basket that got the UFC CEO and President out of his seat and singing the Chechen fighter's praises. Nolan arrives having won four straight, with the Dante Rivera protege having most recently claimed the CFFC welterweight title with a first-round stoppage win in late May. Gerald Meerschaert vs Michal Oleksiejczuk Gerald Meerschaert and Michal Oleksiejczuk meet in this pairing of middleweight mainstays that surprisingly hasn’t been booked before. Your Full Guide To UFC 319 Fight Week A dangerous submission ace with heaps of experience and a 100-percent finishing rate inside the Octagon, Meerschaert arrives in Chicago having suffered consecutive losses to Reinier de Ridder and Brad Tavares. Oleksiejczuk snapped a three-fight slide back in April, venturing to Sao Paulo to train with former opponent Caio Borralho and the Fighting Nerds before storming through Sedriques Dumas in Miami. Jessica Andrade vs Loopy Godinez Strawweight rankings staples Jessica Andrade and Loopy Godinez square off in what profiles as a bit of a crossroads fight for both women. Andrade is both 2-0 in her last two strawweight appearances and coming into this fight on a two-fight skid, having bounced back up to flyweight last year following her win at UFC 300, dropping consecutive bouts to top contenders Natalia Silva and Jasmine Jasudavicius. Godinez was on a real good run through 2023, posting four straight wins and looking like a dark horse in the division, only to drop consecutive divisions to Virna Jandiroba and Mackenzie Dern before bouncing back with a win over Julia Polastri in Mexico City earlier this year. Chase Hooper vs Alexander Hernandez Chase Hooper and Alexander Hernandez share the Octagon in the first of four televised preliminary card bouts this weekend at United Center. Hooper has gone 5-0 since moving to lightweight, most recently getting the better of veteran Jim Miller at UFC 314 in April, while Hernandez has earned back-to-back wins and four straight wins when competing at 155 pounds. This is a “which one moves forward” matchup that should answer a lot of questions about both men once they step in and start to get after it on Saturday evening in Chicago. Edson Barboza vs Drakkar Klose Veterans Edson Barboza and Drakkar Klose line up opposite one another in a bout that feels like a sure-fire barnburner for as long as it lasts. Despite being 39 and well over a dozen years into his UFC tenure, Barboza remains fundamentally sharp and lightning quick with his striking, and it will be interesting to see how that holds up as he moves back to lightweight for the first time since September 2019. Klose has constantly found himself near the rankings, but never quite broke through, as untimely losses have marred what has otherwise been a largely successful career inside the Octagon. Bryan Battle vs Nursulton Ruziboev Former TUF winner Bryan Battle returns to middleweight to face off with Uzbekistani bruiser Nursulton Ruziboev in this low-key banger early in the lineup. Battle earned victories in each of his first two UFC appearances at middleweight before movingdown to welterweight, and he makes his return to the 185-pound ranks riding a five-fight unbeaten streak. Ruziboev opened his UFC run with a pair of finishes before dropping down to welterweight, dropping a decision to Joaquin Buckley, and then returning to middleweight, where he’s since posted two more wins. Karine Silva vs Dione Barbosa Brazilian flyweights Karine Silva and Dione Barbosa meet for the second time in their careers, with each heading into this one with something to prove. Silva had her nine-fight winning streak snapped by another Brazilian, Viviane Araujo, last time out at UFC 309, while Barbosa picked up a Performance of the Night bonus for her submission win over Diana Belbita in April. These two fought all the way back in May 2019, with Barbosa earning a unanimous decision victory, so we’ll have to see if there are lingering tensions between the two as they renew acquaintances on Saturday. Joseph Morales vs Alibi Idiris Morales went 1-2 in his first stint on the UFC roster, but has gone 3-0 since and shown his experience and grit during the competition to punch his ticket to the finale. Unbeaten in 11 pro fights, Idiris won a hard-fought battle against Furkatbek Yokubov in the quarterfinals before knocking out Roybert Echeverria in the semis to earn this opportunity. The night is finally upon us where we get to see du Plessis face off against Chimaev in one of the most highly-anticipated title fights in recent memory. While most of the buzz around this event is getting to see if “Borz” can fulfill his championship dreams after terrorizing the division, du Plessis wants to make it known that he is the headliner, he is the champion, and until someone can stop him it will remain that way. Currently on an 11-fight win streak, “Stillknocks” is undefeated inside the Octagon at 9-0 with two title defenses, including racking up huge wins over Sean Strickland (twice), Robert Whittaker, and Israel Adesanya. His unorthodox style makes him a human puzzle that has yet to be solved by UFC’s best, and it’s a strategy he will need against Chimaev, who is one of the most aggressive fighters in the game. A win for du Plessis will set him further apart from the pack and move him up the pound-for-pound rankings. And taking out the mythical being that is Chimaev, in the process, won’t hurt his stock, either. Since making his UFC debut in 2020, Chimaev has only competed eight times, much to the chagrin of UFC officials and fans alike. But during that time, “Borz” has made the most of his experience inside the cage. From earning two finishes in his first two fights under the UFC banner 10 days apart, going to war with Gilbert Burns in an epic battle, manhandling Kevin Holland and busting up Robert Whittaker’s entire grill, Chimaev has made a big impression to say the least. That’s why he has quickly become a fan-favorite, an enigma of sorts, because people still don’t know how great he truly can be due to his inactivity. But that can all change tonight as the undefeated (17-0, 8-0 UFC) Chechen fighter can put the cherry on top of his terrorizing and violent run by wrapping UFC gold around his waist. He is one of the most aggressive and fast-paced fighters in the game, which may not be the best strategy against the champ. Why? Well, du Plessis has shown to have a great gas tank, and if Chimaev blows his load in the first round trying to get a finish, it could prove to be a long night for him because he’s never gone past the third round in his entire career. Still, this fight could prove to be an all-out slugfest that will be a feast for fight fans around the world. Buckle up. What’s Not: There really isn’t a whole lot to complain about when it comes to this card. It’s well-rounded from top to bottom (despite several changes), though perhaps adding another title fight would’ve been the cherry on top. Original Card Vs. Actual Card: Aaron Pico was in line to face Mosvar Evloev at this event before the promotion switched gears and matched him up against Lerone Murphy, instead. A women’s Flyweight bout between Karine Silva and JJ Aldrich was scheduled for this event before Aldrich withdrew for undisclosed reasons. She was ultimately replaced by Dione Barbosa, who is coming off a submission win over Diana Belbita. As for Silva, she saw her nine-fight win steak come to an end at the hands of Viviane Araujo in her last bout. Injuries: A last-minute injury suffered by King Green cancelled his fight against Diego Ferreira, which was set to be the featured fight on the undercard (read more about it here). Bryan Battle missed weight by four pounds, and as a result his scheduled fight against Nursulton Ruziboev was scratched. Also, a fight between Rodrigo Sezinando and Daniil Donchenko was axed due to a mysterious injury to one of the fighters. New Blood: Speaking of Pico, the former Bellator MMA standout will finally get his chance to make his UFC debut after a small delay as a co-headliner on a major PPV card. Pico signed with the promotion this past April after Bellator MMA went belly up. Once touted as the best prospect in all of MMA, Pico got off to a rough start to his career, losing his MMA debut in 2017. Since then, Pico has been pretty steady with the wins (all under Bellator), going 13-4 with the promotion. He was never able to fight for Bellator gold, but he intends to make an impression right away in order to quickly infiltrate the Top 10 and expedite his shot at a title. He will have a stiff test in the form of undefeated contender, Lerone Murphy. “The Miracle” is 16-0-1 (8-0-1 UFC) and has proven to be one of the more promising rising stars at 145 pounds. With a win over Pico, he shoots up the rankings and his stick takes a tremendous boost to set him up for a potential title run. For Pico, handing Murphy his first loss will make an emphatic statement to the division. He just has to be careful he doesn’t suffer the same fate as his former Bellator stablemate. How The ‘Prelims’ Look: Two struggling Middleweights will collide as Gerald Meerschaert (who was one of Chimaev’s early victims) will face off against Michal Oleksiejczuk. Meerschaert is currently on a two-fight losing streak, while Oleksiejczuk is 1-3 in his last four fights inside the Octagon, though he is coming off a much-needed win over Sedriques Dumas earlier this year at UFC 314 (see it again here). Edson Barboza is still trucking along after 15 years with the promotion. His two-fight win streak came to an end after he ran into Lerone Murphy over a year ago. Now, he will look to shake off the ring rust in his comeback bout against Drakkar Klose, who saw his four-fight win streak evaporate into thin air after Joel Alvarez knocked him out late last year. Both men are in need of a win, and when you couple that with the fact that these two love to stand-and-bang, and we are all in for a treat. Chase Hooper has quietly won five straight fights and is eying lucky No. 6 as he goes head-to-head against Alexander Hernandez. Hooper is really coming into his own after a rough stretch from 2020-2022, and another win could get him into the Top 15. As for Hernandez, he is searching for his first-ever three-fight win streak under the UFC banner, and stopping Hooper’s run will be a big boost for his career, which hasn’t really taken off. Who Needs A Win Badly: Jessica Andrade was once sitting pretty at the top of the women’s Strawweight division as champion and considered one of the best pound-four-pound female fighters in the business. But ever since she ran into the juggernaut that is Zhang Weili over five years ago, her career has been all over the place. She has moved weight classes more times than I care to count, and has a record of 6-8 since 2019. She is currently on a two-fight skid, and if she comes up short against Loopy Godinez, she will be at a crossroads in her MMA career with a lot of questions to answer. Speaking of Loopy, she snapped her own two-fight skid in her previous fight by defeating Julia Polastri. Interest Level: 8/10 In a fight who has the chance to steal the show, Michael Page will battle Jared Cannonier in a Middleweight bout. Page made the jump up to 185 pounds to avoid the politics at 170, defeating Sharabutdin Magomedov earlier this year. “Venom” has long been one of the flashiest and exciting fighters in all of MMA, and he is off to a great start to his UFC career by going 2-1, with his other win coming against Kevin Holland. If he can defeat a former title contender in Cannonier, Page shoots up the rankings and the fights and paychecks get bigger and bigger. He loves to show off hi striking skills, and Cannonier will be more than happy to test him in the standup department. “Killa Gorilla” is coming off a knockout win over Gregory Rodrigues (see it here), which snapped his two-fight losing streak. Do no be surprised if this fight produces post-fight bonus awards. Carlos Prates’ momentum was halted in his last fight after running into Ian Machado Garry earlier this year, snapping his 11-fight win streak while suffering his first UFC loss after racking up four straight knockout wins inside the Octagon. Now, “The Nightmare” is out to start all over against Geoff Neal, who makes his return after a 10-month layoff following his stoppage win over Rafael dos Anjos at UFC 308. Former UFC Flyweight title contender, Tim Elliott, is still trucking right along in his quest to one day reach another title fight. The 14-UFC fight veteran hasn’t been very consistent when it comes to racking up wins over the years, and has never won more than two straight inside the Octagon. He will once again look to secure his second straight win as he faces off against Kai Asakura, who is coming off a champions defeat at the hands of division king, Alexandre Pantoja, at UFC 310. Currently ranked No. 15, Asakura wants to work his way back to another shot at winning UFC gold, and defeating Elliott will be a good step toward that goal, in what will be the first-ever UFC win for the former RIZIN champion. Enjoy the fights! title: Fight By Fight Preview | UFC 319: Du Plessis vs Chimaev
text: The UFC blows into the Windy City for the first time in a little more than six years, returning to the United Center with a packed pay-per-view fight card capped by one of the most highly anticipated bouts of the year. Saturday night’s main event features reigning middleweight champion Dricus Du Plessis defending his title for the second time this year as he steps in with undefeated challenger Khamzat Chimaev, who has been forecasted to reach this position since he first stormed the gates back on Fight Island. Back by a quartet of compelling main card contests and a loaded preliminary card slate, UFC 319 shapes up as one of the deepest, most competitive cards of the year, and we’ve got the goods on what to expect when the action hits the Octagon this weekend below. Main Event: Dricus Du Plessis vs Khamzat Chimaev Location: United Center — Chicago, IL Where to Watch: ESPN+ / Disney+ Other Main Card Matches: Order UFC 319: Du Plessis vs Chimaev Prelim Matches: MIDDLEWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP MAIN EVENT Dricus Du Plessis vs Khamzat Chimaev Middleweight champ Dricus Du Plessis looks to defend his place atop the division once more as he welcomes the challenge of unbeaten marauder Khamzat Chimaev in the UFC 319 main event. The South African titleholder continues to deliver more dominant performances and eliminate room for questioning his standing as the best middleweight in the world with each successive outing. He earned his second successful title defense earlier this year by thoroughly outworking former champ Sean Strickland in a rematch of their UFC 297 encounter, which extended Du Plessis’ record to 9-0 in the UFC and 23-2 overall. Five years after exploding onto the scene with three wins in two months, Chimaev finally lands in his first championship fight, aiming to maintain his unblemished record while proving he’s every bit the unstoppable force many have long believed him to be. The now 31-year-old standout secured this opportunity with a first-round submission win over Robert Whittaker last October that was closer to a mugging than a competitive matchup, and silenced any questions about his health or his ability to hang with the very best in the world. GET YOUR TICKETS: UFC 319 | UFC Shanghai | UFC Paris This is an absolutely fascinating matchup because despite all their successes, there are questions that remain on both sides and cases to be made in favor of each man. More than any fight either has engaged in to this point, Saturday’s main event is going to be the proving ground for both Du Plessis and Chimaev, and have an unquestionable impact on how we look at each in the present and going forward. This is going to be special. ADDITIONAL MAIN CARD MATCHUPS Lerone Murphy vs Aaron Pico Lerone Murphy puts his undefeated record on the line as he welcomes Aaron Pico to the Octagon for the first time in this outstanding featherweight fixture. There are a lot of similarities between Murphy and fellow Brit Leon Edwards, who steadily worked his way to the top of the welterweight division as, like the former welterweight ruler, the 34-year-old Manchester man is on an outstanding run of success without much fanfare, and is without question a better fighter than most understand or give him credit for being. Over his last three fights, “The Miracle” has earned quality wins over Edson Barboza, Dan Ige, and Josh Emmett to cement his standing as a contender, and vanquishing Pico would certainly strengthen his case for a championship opportunity early next year. Now 28 years old, Pico has grown into being the fighter most envisioned when he was a teenage phenom that had yet to actually make the transition into mixed martial arts, though some questions do still linger. He’s gone 9-1 over his last 10 fights, with his only loss coming as a result of an injury, and has a complete assortment of tools at his disposal, including proven knockout power and excellent wrestling. Murphy is the established, entrenched half of this pairing, though he still has room to ascend in terms of acceptance and recognition, and a win here would definitely help that cause. For Pico, this is his chance to catapult himself right into the thick of the title chase and show that he’s more than capable of running with the elites in the UFC featherweight division. Geoff Neal vs Carlos Prates Originally scheduled to face off at UFC 314 in Miami, Geoff Neal and Carlos Prates command the feature slot on Saturday’s talent-rich main card. Neal, who turns 35 less than two weeks after this weekend’s event, competes for the first time since his abbreviated bout with Rafael Dos Anjos last October in Abu Dhabi, which was halted when the former lightweight champ suffered a knee injury. The Fortis MMA representative has been a Top 15 staple for the last several years, settling into life in the 6-12 range, while showcasing sharp, punishing hands and the tenacity and moxie to push both Shavkat Rakhmanov and Ian Machado Garry to their limits. WATCH: UFC 319 Embedded Following a breakout rookie campaign where he went 4-0 with four finishes to force his way into the rankings, Prates suffered his first loss in a dozen fights last time out, dropping a decision to Machado Garry in a fight where the Irish standout was strategic for the majority ofthe contest before getting in a little trouble late. If the Fighting Nerds’ core four — Caio Borralho, Jean Silva, Mauricio Ruffy, and Prates — were the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Prates would be Raphael, the somewhat volatile, ever-dangerous member of the group, which is what makes him a constant threat, captivating to watch, and susceptible to missteps like the one he experienced in Kansas City against Machado Garry. It’s highly likely that these two wade into the center, touch gloves, and start throwing fastballs at one another straight away, stopping only when the horn sounds signaling the end of the round or one of them is left staring up at the lights. Buckle up and enjoy because this one is sure to be electric. Jared Cannonier vs Michael Page Middleweight has been having a moment here, and before the title goes up for grabs, Jared Cannonier and Michael Page will stand opposite one another with a place in the Top 10 hanging in the balance. A Top 10 mainstay since he debuted in the division towards the end of 2018, Cannonier halted a two-fight slide earlier this year by rallying to finish Gregory Rodrigues. Now 26 fights into his career and at “Level 41,” the MMA Lab product is the perfect top-end measuring stick in a weight class that has been undergoing some changes over the last two years, as the only people to best him at middleweight remain former champs Robert Whittaker and Israel Adesanya, and upcoming Paris headliners Nassourdine Imavov and Caio Borralho, who could very well be fighting to determine who faces Saturday’s title fight winner. BREAKING: Paramount and TKO Announce Historic UFC Media Rights Agreement Page bounced up to middleweight earlier this year to bounce Shara Magomedov from the ranks of the unbeaten, showing that he’s the better range fighter of the two and still a tricky puzzle to solve for whomever stands across from him inside the Octagon. While he’s now 38 years old, “MVP” feels like he’s capable of having an extended twilight similar to that of Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson, who has remained a Top 15 fighter well into his 40s. This one is all going to come down to how Cannonier opts to approach things, as it feels like there is a clear blueprint for how to neutralize Page. Typically, “The Killa Gorilla” isn’t someone that looks to wrestle all that much, so we should get plenty of striking exchanges in space, where it will be Cannonier’s power against Page’s speed and variety. Tim Elliott vs Kai Asakura Saturday’s main card kicks off with an intriguing pairing in the flyweight division as former title challengers Tim Elliott and Kai Asakura go head-to-head in Chicago. Nearly a decade removed from his competitive title bout with Demetrious Johnson, Elliott has remained one of the top veteran tests in the 125-pound weight class, posting a 7-6 record over his last 13 starts, most of which have come against the division’s best. He hasn’t fought since submitting Sumudaerji in December 2023, so it will be interesting to see how the 38-year-old looks after such an extended absence. Asakura got an immediate title shot last December after joining the UFC from RIZIN, stepping into a bout with Alexandre Pantoja where he fell by submission in the second round. The Japanese fighter rose to prominence on the strength of quality wins over Manel Kape and KyojiHoriguchi, as well as his explosive power, and he gets a second chance to make a first impression in the Octagon. PRELIMINARY CARD PAIRINGS Baisangur Susurkaev vs Eric Nolan Four days after earning his place on the UFC roster, Baisangur Susurkaev gets his wish to compete this weekend alongside training partner Khamzat Chimaev as he takes on New Jersey native Eric Nolan at UFC 319. Susurkaev earned the lone finish on Tuesday's opening episode of Dana White's Contender Series, finishing returning hopeful Murtaza Talha with a front kick to the bread basket that got the UFC CEO and President out of his seat and singing the Chechen fighter's praises. Nolan arrives having won four straight, with the Dante Rivera protege having most recently claimed the CFFC welterweight title with a first-round stoppage win in late May. Gerald Meerschaert vs Michal Oleksiejczuk Gerald Meerschaert and Michal Oleksiejczuk meet in this pairing of middleweight mainstays that surprisingly hasn’t been booked before. Your Full Guide To UFC 319 Fight Week A dangerous submission ace with heaps of experience and a 100-percent finishing rate inside the Octagon, Meerschaert arrives in Chicago having suffered consecutive losses to Reinier de Ridder and Brad Tavares. Oleksiejczuk snapped a three-fight slide back in April, venturing to Sao Paulo to train with former opponent Caio Borralho and the Fighting Nerds before storming through Sedriques Dumas in Miami. Jessica Andrade vs Loopy Godinez Strawweight rankings staples Jessica Andrade and Loopy Godinez square off in what profiles as a bit of a crossroads fight for both women. Andrade is both 2-0 in her last two strawweight appearances and coming into this fight on a two-fight skid, having bounced back up to flyweight last year following her win at UFC 300, dropping consecutive bouts to top contenders Natalia Silva and Jasmine Jasudavicius. Godinez was on a real good run through 2023, posting four straight wins and looking like a dark horse in the division, only to drop consecutive divisions to Virna Jandiroba and Mackenzie Dern before bouncing back with a win over Julia Polastri in Mexico City earlier this year. Chase Hooper vs Alexander Hernandez Chase Hooper and Alexander Hernandez share the Octagon in the first of four televised preliminary card bouts this weekend at United Center. Hooper has gone 5-0 since moving to lightweight, most recently getting the better of veteran Jim Miller at UFC 314 in April, while Hernandez has earned back-to-back wins and four straight wins when competing at 155 pounds. This is a “which one moves forward” matchup that should answer a lot of questions about both men once they step in and start to get after it on Saturday evening in Chicago. Edson Barboza vs Drakkar Klose Veterans Edson Barboza and Drakkar Klose line up opposite one another in a bout that feels like a sure-fire barnburner for as long as it lasts. Despite being 39 and well over a dozen years into his UFC tenure, Barboza remains fundamentally sharp and lightning quick with his striking, and it will be interesting to see how that holds up as he moves back to lightweight for the first time since September 2019. Klose has constantly found himself near the rankings, but never quite broke through, as untimely losses have marred what has otherwise been a largely successful career inside the Octagon. Bryan Battle vs Nursulton Ruziboev Former TUF winner Bryan Battle returns to middleweight to face off with Uzbekistani bruiser Nursulton Ruziboev in this low-key banger early in the lineup. Battle earned victories in each of his first two UFC appearances at middleweight before movingdown to welterweight, and he makes his return to the 185-pound ranks riding a five-fight unbeaten streak. Ruziboev opened his UFC run with a pair of finishes before dropping down to welterweight, dropping a decision to Joaquin Buckley, and then returning to middleweight, where he’s since posted two more wins. Karine Silva vs Dione Barbosa Brazilian flyweights Karine Silva and Dione Barbosa meet for the second time in their careers, with each heading into this one with something to prove. Silva had her nine-fight winning streak snapped by another Brazilian, Viviane Araujo, last time out at UFC 309, while Barbosa picked up a Performance of the Night bonus for her submission win over Diana Belbita in April. These two fought all the way back in May 2019, with Barbosa earning a unanimous decision victory, so we’ll have to see if there are lingering tensions between the two as they renew acquaintances on Saturday. Joseph Morales vs Alibi Idiris Morales went 1-2 in his first stint on the UFC roster, but has gone 3-0 since and shown his experience and grit during the competition to punch his ticket to the finale. Unbeaten in 11 pro fights, Idiris won a hard-fought battle against Furkatbek Yokubov in the quarterfinals before knocking out Roybert Echeverria in the semis to earn this opportunity. Don't miss a moment of UFC 319: Du Plessis vs Chimaev, live from United Center in Chicago, Illinois on August 16, 2025. Prelims start at 8pm ET/5pm PT, followed by the main card live on PPV at 10pm ET/7pm PT.

text: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is back on the pay-per-view (PPV) market (but it won’t be free…yet), as UFC 319 is set to go down later TONIGHT (Sat. Aug. 16, 2025) inside United Center in Chicago, Illinois on ESPN+. Headlining the event will be a Middleweight title fight as division champion, Dricus du Plessis, will defend against the boogeyman of the division, Khamzat Chimaev. In the co-main event, Aaron Pico will make his UFC debut against Lerone Murphy in what is sure-to-be a hard-hitting Featherweight affair. What’s Hot: UFC 319 CHEAT SHEET What UFC event is on tonight? UFC 319: “du Plessis vs. Chimaev” Who is fighting tonight at UFC 319? Dricus du Plessis vs. Khamzat Chimaev Middleweight title fight is the five-round main event. What time does UFC 319? TONIGHT (Sat., Aug. 16, 2025), beginning at 6:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Where will UFC 319 take place? United Center in Chicago, Illinois. How can I watch UFC 319? The early ESPN+ “Prelims” bouts scheduled for 6:30 p.m. ET, then the remaining undercard balance on ESPN/ESPN+ at 8 p.m. ET, followed by the PPV main card start time at 10 p.m. ET on ESPN+ PPV. How do I bet on UFC 319? Checkout the latest lines at DraftKings.com Where can I get UFC 319 updates and results? Get full UFC 319 play-by-play updates and live coverage here! The night is finally upon us where we get to see du Plessis face off against Chimaev in one of the most highly-anticipated title fights in recent memory. While most of the buzz around this event is getting to see if “Borz” can fulfill his championship dreams after terrorizing the division, du Plessis wants to make it known that he is the headliner, he is the champion, and until someone can stop him it will remain that way. Currently on an 11-fight win streak, “Stillknocks” is undefeated inside the Octagon at 9-0 with two title defenses, including racking up huge wins over Sean Strickland (twice), Robert Whittaker, and Israel Adesanya. His unorthodox style makes him a human puzzle that has yet to be solved by UFC’s best, and it’s a strategy he will need against Chimaev, who is one of the most aggressive fighters in the game. A win for du Plessis will set him further apart from the pack and move him up the pound-for-pound rankings. And taking out the mythical being that is Chimaev, in the process, won’t hurt his stock, either. Since making his UFC debut in 2020, Chimaev has only competed eight times, much to the chagrin of UFC officials and fans alike. But during that time, “Borz” has made the most of his experience inside the cage. From earning two finishes in his first two fights under the UFC banner 10 days apart, going to war with Gilbert Burns in an epic battle, manhandling Kevin Holland and busting up Robert Whittaker’s entire grill, Chimaev has made a big impression to say the least. That’s why he has quickly become a fan-favorite, an enigma of sorts, because people still don’t know how great he truly can be due to his inactivity. But that can all change tonight as the undefeated (17-0, 8-0 UFC) Chechen fighter can put the cherry on top of his terrorizing and violent run by wrapping UFC gold around his waist. He is one of the most aggressive and fast-paced fighters in the game, which may not be the best strategy against the champ. Why? Well, du Plessis has shown to have a great gas tank, and if Chimaev blows his load in the first round trying to get a finish, it could prove to be a long night for him because he’s never gone past the third round in his entire career. Still, this fight could prove to be an all-out slugfest that will be a feast for fight fans around the world. Buckle up. What’s Not: There really isn’t a whole lot to complain about when it comes to this card. It’s well-rounded from top to bottom (despite several changes), though perhaps adding another title fight would’ve been the cherry on top. Original Card Vs. Actual Card: Aaron Pico was in line to face Mosvar Evloev at this event before the promotion switched gears and matched him up against Lerone Murphy, instead. A women’s Flyweight bout between Karine Silva and JJ Aldrich was scheduled for this event before Aldrich withdrew for undisclosed reasons. She was ultimately replaced by Dione Barbosa, who is coming off a submission win over Diana Belbita. As for Silva, she saw her nine-fight win steak come to an end at the hands of Viviane Araujo in her last bout. Injuries: A last-minute injury suffered by King Green cancelled his fight against Diego Ferreira, which was set to be the featured fight on the undercard (read more about it here). Bryan Battle missed weight by four pounds, and as a result his scheduled fight against Nursulton Ruziboev was scratched. Also, a fight between Rodrigo Sezinando and Daniil Donchenko was axed due to a mysterious injury to one of the fighters. New Blood: Speaking of Pico, the former Bellator MMA standout will finally get his chance to make his UFC debut after a small delay as a co-headliner on a major PPV card. Pico signed with the promotion this past April after Bellator MMA went belly up. Once touted as the best prospect in all of MMA, Pico got off to a rough start to his career, losing his MMA debut in 2017. Since then, Pico has been pretty steady with the wins (all under Bellator), going 13-4 with the promotion. He was never able to fight for Bellator gold, but he intends to make an impression right away in order to quickly infiltrate the Top 10 and expedite his shot at a title. He will have a stiff test in the form of undefeated contender, Lerone Murphy. “The Miracle” is 16-0-1 (8-0-1 UFC) and has proven to be one of the more promising rising stars at 145 pounds. With a win over Pico, he shoots up the rankings and his stick takes a tremendous boost to set him up for a potential title run. For Pico, handing Murphy his first loss will make an emphatic statement to the division. He just has to be careful he doesn’t suffer the same fate as his former Bellator stablemate. How The ‘Prelims’ Look: Two struggling Middleweights will collide as Gerald Meerschaert (who was one of Chimaev’s early victims) will face off against Michal Oleksiejczuk. Meerschaert is currently on a two-fight losing streak, while Oleksiejczuk is 1-3 in his last four fights inside the Octagon, though he is coming off a much-needed win over Sedriques Dumas earlier this year at UFC 314 (see it again here). Edson Barboza is still trucking along after 15 years with the promotion. His two-fight win streak came to an end after he ran into Lerone Murphy over a year ago. Now, he will look to shake off the ring rust in his comeback bout against Drakkar Klose, who saw his four-fight win streak evaporate into thin air after Joel Alvarez knocked him out late last year. Both men are in need of a win, and when you couple that with the fact that these two love to stand-and-bang, and we are all in for a treat. Chase Hooper has quietly won five straight fights and is eying lucky No. 6 as he goes head-to-head against Alexander Hernandez. Hooper is really coming into his own after a rough stretch from 2020-2022, and another win could get him into the Top 15. As for Hernandez, he is searching for his first-ever three-fight win streak under the UFC banner, and stopping Hooper’s run will be a big boost for his career, which hasn’t really taken off. Who Needs A Win Badly: Jessica Andrade was once sitting pretty at the top of the women’s Strawweight division as champion and considered one of the best pound-four-pound female fighters in the business. But ever since she ran into the juggernaut that is Zhang Weili over five years ago, her career has been all over the place. She has moved weight classes more times than I care to count, and has a record of 6-8 since 2019. She is currently on a two-fight skid, and if she comes up short against Loopy Godinez, she will be at a crossroads in her MMA career with a lot of questions to answer. Speaking of Loopy, she snapped her own two-fight skid in her previous fight by defeating Julia Polastri. Interest Level: 8/10 In a fight who has the chance to steal the show, Michael Page will battle Jared Cannonier in a Middleweight bout. Page made the jump up to 185 pounds to avoid the politics at 170, defeating Sharabutdin Magomedov earlier this year. “Venom” has long been one of the flashiest and exciting fighters in all of MMA, and he is off to a great start to his UFC career by going 2-1, with his other win coming against Kevin Holland. If he can defeat a former title contender in Cannonier, Page shoots up the rankings and the fights and paychecks get bigger and bigger. He loves to show off hi striking skills, and Cannonier will be more than happy to test him in the standup department. “Killa Gorilla” is coming off a knockout win over Gregory Rodrigues (see it here), which snapped his two-fight losing streak. Do no be surprised if this fight produces post-fight bonus awards. Carlos Prates’ momentum was halted in his last fight after running into Ian Machado Garry earlier this year, snapping his 11-fight win streak while suffering his first UFC loss after racking up four straight knockout wins inside the Octagon. Now, “The Nightmare” is out to start all over against Geoff Neal, who makes his return after a 10-month layoff following his stoppage win over Rafael dos Anjos at UFC 308. Former UFC Flyweight title contender, Tim Elliott, is still trucking right along in his quest to one day reach another title fight. The 14-UFC fight veteran hasn’t been very consistent when it comes to racking up wins over the years, and has never won more than two straight inside the Octagon. He will once again look to secure his second straight win as he faces off against Kai Asakura, who is coming off a champions defeat at the hands of division king, Alexandre Pantoja, at UFC 310. Currently ranked No. 15, Asakura wants to work his way back to another shot at winning UFC gold, and defeating Elliott will be a good step toward that goal, in what will be the first-ever UFC win for the former RIZIN champion. Enjoy the fights! text: Chase Hooper: From Alexander Hernandez Rivalry to Future MMA Prospects Introduction: The Rise of Chase Hooper Chase Hooper, a name quickly becoming synonymous with young talent and exciting grappling in mixed martial arts (MMA), has carved a unique path in the sport. From his early days as a prodigy on the regional scene to his current presence in the UFC, Hooper's journey is a testament to dedication, evolving skill sets, and a willingness to learn and adapt. Early Career and Regional Dominance Hooper's ascent to the UFC was rapid, fueled by a combination of impressive performances and a dedicated online following. Even before turning professional, videos showcasing his grappling prowess circulated widely, earning him attention and the moniker of a prodigy. He started his professional career at a young age, facing older, more experienced opponents on the regional circuit. These early fights, while not always flawless victories, provided invaluable experience and exposure. The regional scene served as a crucial proving ground, allowing Hooper to hone his skills and develop a more well-rounded game before stepping onto the biggest stage in MMA. The Alexander Hernandez Rivalry: A Defining Moment The fight against Alexander Hernandez at UFC Fight Night: Font vs. Vera in April 2023 stands as a critical moment in Chase Hooper's career. Hernandez, a seasoned veteran known for his striking and aggressive style, presented a significant test for the young Hooper. This fight was more than just another bout; it represented a clash of styles, experience levels, and career trajectories. Pre-Fight Expectations and Analysis Leading up to the fight, many analysts considered Hernandez a heavy favorite. His striking power and experience were seen as significant advantages. However, Hooper's grappling skills were acknowledged as a potential equalizer. The prevailing narrative suggested that if Hooper could weather the early storm and take the fight to the ground, he would have a path to victory. Conversely, if Hernandez could keep the fight standing and utilize his striking, he was likely to secure a finish. The Fight Breakdown The fight unfolded largely as predicted. Hernandez came out aggressively, landing significant strikes in the opening rounds. Hooper absorbed considerable damage but remained composed and resilient. His ability to withstand Hernandez's initial onslaught was crucial. As the fight progressed, Hooper began to implement his grappling game, securing takedowns and working for submissions. The turning point came when Hooper locked in an arm-triangle choke, forcing Hernandez to tap out in the third round. This victory was not just a win; it was a statement. Analyzing the Keys to Victory Several factors contributed to Hooper's victory over Hernandez: - **Resilience and Chin:** Hooper demonstrated remarkable resilience, absorbing significant strikes without being deterred. - **Grappling Prowess:** His ability to secure takedowns and transition into advantageous positions on the ground proved decisive. - **Submission Skills:** The arm-triangle choke showcased his refined submission skills and ability to capitalize on opportunities. - **Game Plan Execution:** Hooper and his team clearly had a well-defined game plan, which they executed effectively despite facing adversity. Impact on Hooper's Career Trajectory The victory over Hernandez significantly boosted Hooper's stock in the UFC. It demonstrated his ability to overcome adversity, execute a game plan against a dangerous opponent, and secure a meaningful victory. It also silenced many doubters who questioned his ability to compete against established veterans. This win served as a springboard, opening doors to higher-profile fights and greater opportunities. Strengths and Weaknesses: A Detailed Assessment To accurately project Hooper's future prospects, it is essential to conduct a thorough assessment of his strengths and weaknesses. This analysis will provide a foundation for understanding his potential for growth and the areas where he needs to improve. Strengths - **Exceptional Grappling:** Hooper's grappling is undoubtedly his greatest strength. His submission skills, takedown ability, and ground control are all exceptionally high. He is particularly adept at utilizing various chokes and leg locks. - **Submission Variety:** Hooper displays a wide array of submission techniques, making him difficult to predict and prepare for on the ground. - **Resilience:** As demonstrated in the Hernandez fight, Hooper possesses remarkable resilience and the ability to withstand punishment. - **Cardio:** Hooper's cardiovascular conditioning is consistently strong, allowing him to maintain a high pace throughout his fights. - **Adaptability:** He has shown the ability to adapt his game plan mid-fight, adjusting to his opponent's strengths and weaknesses. - **Youth and Potential:** At a relatively young age, Hooper has significant room for improvement and development. - **Aggressive Style:** His willingness to engage and pursue finishes makes him an exciting fighter to watch. Weaknesses - **Striking Defense:** Hooper's striking defense is an area that needs improvement. He has shown a tendency to absorb too much damage on the feet. - **Striking Power:** While his striking has improved, Hooper is not known for possessing significant knockout power. - **Takedown Defense:** While his grappling is strong, his takedown defense can be vulnerable at times. - **Decision Making Under Pressure:** In some fights, Hooper's decision-making under pressure has been questionable. - **Sometimes Starts Slow:** Occasionally, Hooper starts slow and allows his opponent to dictate the pace of the fight early on. These areas include: - **Striking Defense:** Focusing on head movement, footwork, and blocking techniques to minimize damage taken on the feet. - **Striking Power:** Developing more power in his strikes through improved technique and strength training. - **Takedown Defense:** Enhancing his takedown defense through drills and specialized training to prevent opponents from taking him down. - **Fight IQ and Decision Making:** Improving his fight IQ and decision-making through film study, sparring, and working with experienced coaches. - **Early Fight Aggression:** Developing a strategy to start fights more aggressively and dictate the pace from the outset. Addressing these areas will require a dedicated training regimen, incorporating elements of striking, wrestling, and grappling. Working with a skilled coaching team is essential to ensure that the training is effective and tailored to Hooper's specific needs. Potential Matchups and Future Opponents Considering Hooper's current standing in the UFC and his skill set, several potential matchups could prove to be exciting and beneficial for his career. This fight would test Hooper's takedown defense and ability to impose his grappling game against a skilled wrestler. - **Dan Hooker:** Hooker, known for his aggressive striking and toughness, would be a stand-up war for Hooper. This fight would test Hooper's striking defense and his ability to withstand punishment. - **Nasrat Haqparast:** Haqparast, a powerful striker with a developing grappling game, would provide a well-rounded test for Hooper. These are just a few examples, and the specific matchups will depend on various factors, including the UFC's matchmaking decisions, the availability of opponents, and Hooper's own preferences. However, these potential opponents represent the type of challenges that Hooper will need to overcome to advance in the division. Projecting Future Success: Long-Term Potential Evaluating Hooper's long-term potential requires considering his age, skill set, work ethic, and the evolving landscape of the UFC. While predicting the future in MMA is inherently difficult, several factors suggest that Hooper has the potential to achieve significant success in the sport. Factors Supporting Future Success - **Youth and Development:** Hooper's young age provides him with ample time to continue developing his skills and evolving as a fighter. - **Dedication and Work Ethic:** His commitment to training and his willingness to learn and adapt are crucial for long-term success. - **Strong Grappling Base:** His exceptional grappling skills provide a solid foundation for his MMA game. - **Growing Fanbase:** His dedicated fanbase provides him with support and motivation. - **Adaptability:** Showing the ability to adjust his game plan mid-fight, adjusting to his opponent's strengths and weaknesses. Realistic Expectations While Hooper has the potential to achieve significant success, it is important to maintain realistic expectations. Becoming a champion in the UFC is an extremely difficult feat, and only a small percentage of fighters ever reach that level. However, with continued hard work, dedication, and smart decision-making, Hooper has the potential to become a top contender and a perennial presence in the upper echelons of the division. It’s also realistic to see him become a consistent top 15 ranked fighter. Given the depth of talent at lightweight, this would still be considered a major achievement for someone so young. Conclusion: A Promising Future Chase Hooper's journey in MMA has been marked by rapid progress, significant victories, and a relentless pursuit of improvement. His win over Alexander Hernandez served as a pivotal moment, showcasing his resilience, grappling prowess, and ability to execute a game plan against a dangerous opponent. While he still has areas to improve upon, his youth, dedication, and exceptional grappling skills suggest a promising future in the sport. As he continues to develop and refine his game, Hooper has the potential to become a top contender in the UFC and a significant force in the lightweight division. His journey is one of dedication, growth, and potential, and it will be fascinating to watch his career unfold.

He currently competes in the Lightweight division of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). Mixed martial arts career [edit]Hooper began his amateur MMA career while he was still attending Enumclaw High School.[4] On the regional circuit of Washington, Hooper compiled an undefeated 5–0 record with four stoppage wins[5] before making his professional debut on October 7, 2017, against Edson Penado. Hooper won the fight via rear-naked choke submission in the first round[6] utilizing his heavy skills in Brazilian jiu-jitsu, in which he's a juvenile Pan American champion as a blue belt.[7] Dana White's Contender Series [edit]Hooper competed at Dana White's Contender Series 14 against Canaan Kawaihae. He won the fight via unanimous decision and was awarded a development league contract.[8] He competed in three more fights (winning two of them and the other one ending in a draw) in notable minor promotions such as CFFC and Titan FC before being signed by the UFC.[9] Ultimate Fighting Championships [edit]Hooper made his promotional debut against Daniel Teymur on December 14, 2019, at UFC 245. He won the fight via technical knockout in the first round.[10] Hooper faced Alex Caceres on June 6, 2020, at UFC 250.[11] He lost the fight via unanimous decision, marking his first professional defeat.[12] Hooper faced Peter Barrett at UFC 256 on December 12, 2020.[13] He earned a comeback win in the third round via heel hook submission.[14] Hooper faced Steven Peterson on June 12, 2021, at UFC 263.[15] At the weigh-ins, Peterson weighed in at 148.5 pounds, two and a half pounds over the featherweight non-title fight limit. The bout proceeded at catchweight and he was fined 20% of his purse, which went to Hooper.[16] Hooper lost the fight via unanimous decision.[17] Hooper faced Felipe Colares on May 21, 2022, at UFC Fight Night 206.[18] He won the fight via technical knockout in round three.[19] This win earned him the Performance of the Night award.[20] Hooper faced Steve Garcia on October 29, 2022, at UFC Fight From his early days as a prodigy on the regional scene to his current presence in the UFC, Hooper's journey is a testament to dedication, evolving skill sets, and a willingness to learn and adapt. This analysis delves into Hooper's career, focusing on his significant rivalry with Alexander Hernandez and projecting his potential future trajectory. Early Career and Regional Dominance Hooper's ascent to the UFC was rapid, fueled by a combination of impressive performances and a dedicated online following. Even before turning professional, videos showcasing his grappling prowess circulated widely, earning him attention and the moniker of a prodigy. He started his professional career at a young age, facing older, more experienced opponents on the regional circuit. These early fights, while not always flawless victories, provided invaluable experience and exposure. The regional scene served as a crucial proving ground, allowing Hooper to hone his skills and develop a more well-rounded game before stepping onto the biggest stage in MMA. The Alexander Hernandez Rivalry: A Defining Moment The fight against Alexander Hernandez at UFC Fight Night: Font vs. Vera in April 2023 stands as a critical moment in Chase Hooper's career. Hernandez, a seasoned veteran known for his striking and aggressive style, presented a significant test for the young Hooper. This fight was more than just another bout; it represented a clash of styles, experience levels, and career trajectories. Pre-Fight Expectations and Analysis Leading up to the fight, many analysts considered Hernandez a heavy favorite. His striking power and experience were seen as significant advantages. Mixed martial arts career [edit]Hooper began his amateur MMA career while he was still attending Enumclaw High School.[4] On the regional circuit of Washington, Hooper compiled an undefeated 5–0 record with four stoppage wins[5] before making his professional debut on October 7, 2017, against Edson Penado. Hooper won the fight via rear-naked choke submission in the first round[6] utilizing his heavy skills in Brazilian jiu-jitsu, in which he's a juvenile Pan American champion as a blue belt.[7] Dana White's Contender Series [edit]Hooper competed at Dana White's Contender Series 14 against Canaan Kawaihae. He won the fight via unanimous decision and was awarded a development league contract.[8] He competed in three more fights (winning two of them and the other one ending in a draw) in notable minor promotions such as CFFC and Titan FC before being signed by the UFC.[9] Ultimate Fighting Championships [edit]Hooper made his promotional debut against Daniel Teymur on December 14, 2019, at UFC 245.
